topic.title: A guide to famous cities
topic.description: Read about three famous world cities to practice scanning for specific details, comparing facts, and answering comprehension questions.

readingPassage.title: Three Great Cities to Visit
readingPassage.text:
London
London is the capital city of the United Kingdom. It is famous for its historical landmarks like Big Ben, the Tower of London, and Buckingham Palace. Millions of tourists visit every year to walk along the River Thames and visit famous museums, which are mostly free to enter.

Tokyo
Tokyo is the bustling capital of Japan. It blends modern technology, high-speed trains, and tall skyscrapers with traditional temples and peaceful gardens. The city is world-famous for its delicious sushi, ramen, and vibrant shopping districts like Shibuya.

Sydney
Sydney is the largest city in Australia. Situated on the coast, it is famous for its iconic Opera House and Harbour Bridge. Visitors love spending hot summer days at Bondi Beach, swimming in the ocean, or trying out surfing lessons.

vocabulary.definition: Famous buildings or structures that are easily recognized.
Full of energetic activity, people, and noise.
Very famous and representative of a particular place or idea.

tips: Scan the headings (city names) first before reading the entire text.
Look for keywords in the questions (like 'museums' or 'beach') and match them with the relevant section.
Pay attention to geographical adjectives (e.g., 'capital', 'coast', 'largest').

topic.title: Are you a good digital citizen?
topic.description: Read a quiz and guidance checklist about safe and responsible internet usage.

readingPassage.title: Digital Citizenship Checklist
readingPassage.text:
Being a good digital citizen means treating others with respect online.
- Always ask permission before posting photos of your friends.
- Never share personal information like your address or passwords.
- Think before you comment: Is it kind? Is it true?
- Report cyberbullying or mean behavior to a trusted adult or site moderator.

tips: Look for modal verbs of obligation and advice (e.g., 'always', 'never', 'must').
Understand safety imperatives for protecting personal data.

exercises.instruction: Decide if the statements represent good digital citizenship.

topic.title: About Earth
topic.description: Read key scientific facts about Planet Earth, its oceans, atmosphere, and continents.

readingPassage.title: Planet Earth Facts
readingPassage.text: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only astronomical object known to harbor life. About 71% of Earth's surface is covered with water, mostly by oceans. The atmosphere consists mostly of nitrogen and oxygen, which protects living organisms from harmful solar radiation and keeps the planet warm through the greenhouse effect.

tips: Pay attention to numerical statistics and percentages.
Identify scientific cause-and-effect relationships.

topic.title: 7 tips for a tidy desk
topic.description: Read practical advice on maintaining a clean and organized study desk workspace.

readingPassage.title: Keep Your Desk Tidy!
readingPassage.text:
1. Only keep items you use every day on your desk.
2. Use pen holders and small boxes for stationery.
3. Keep papers in organized folders instead of piles.
4. Clean your computer screen and keyboard once a week.
5. Put your school bag next to your desk, not on it.
6. Throw away old rubbish at the end of every day.
7. Keep a water bottle nearby to stay hydrated.

tips: Use imperative verbs for organizational rules ('Keep', 'Clean', 'Throw away').
Recognize time frequency words ('every day', 'once a week').

topic.title: Online safety poster

readingPassage.title: Stay Safe Online!
readingPassage.text:
- Create strong passwords combining letters, numbers, and symbols.
- Never share your passwords with friends or classmates.
- Do not click on unknown links or download unexpected attachments.
- Keep your social media accounts private.
- Talk to a parent or teacher if something online makes you uncomfortable.

readingPassage.text: The internet connects millions of computers worldwide. Invented in the late 20th century, it revolutionized how people communicate, work, and learn. Today, people use web browsers to access information, stream videos, play online games, and keep in touch with friends instantly across global distances.

topic.title: Using mind maps
topic.description: Read an educational article explaining how mind mapping helps revision and brain storming.

readingPassage.title: How to Create a Mind Map
readingPassage.text: A mind map is a visual diagram used to organize information. Start by drawing your main idea in the center of a blank page. Draw main branches connecting to sub-topics, using different colors and short key phrases. Adding small pictures or symbols helps your brain remember information much faster!

tips: Follow step-by-step visual creation instructions.
